text:
Which of the following contain the same number of atoms?

(Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{H},\mathrm{He},\mathrm{O}$ and S are 1, 4, 16 and 32 respectively)

A. 2 g of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ gas

B. 4 g of $\mathrm{SO}_{2}$ gas

C. 1400 mL of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ at STP

D. $0.05\mathrm{L}$ of He at STP

E. $0.0625\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number of atoms $=$ moles $\times$ atoms per molecule $\times N_{A}$, with 1 mol of gas at STP taken as $22.4\text{L}$.

A: $n(\mathrm{O}{}_{2})=\dfrac{2}{32}=\dfrac{1}{16}\text{mol}$, so atoms $=\dfrac{1}{16}\times 2N_{A}=\dfrac{N_{A}}{8}$.

B: $n(\mathrm{SO}{}_{2})=\dfrac{4}{64}=\dfrac{1}{16}\text{mol}$, so atoms $=\dfrac{1}{16}\times 3N_{A}=\dfrac{3N_{A}}{16}$.

C: $n(\mathrm{O}{}_{2})=\dfrac{1400}{22400}=\dfrac{1}{16}\text{mol}$, so atoms $=\dfrac{1}{16}\times 2N_{A}=\dfrac{N_{A}}{8}$.

D: $n(\mathrm{He})=\dfrac{0.05}{22.4}\approx 0.0022\text{mol}$, and He is monatomic, so atoms $\approx 0.0022N_{A}$.

E: $n(\mathrm{H}{}_{2})=0.0625=\dfrac{1}{16}\text{mol}$, so atoms $=\dfrac{1}{16}\times 2N_{A}=\dfrac{N_{A}}{8}$.

A, C and E each contain $\dfrac{N_{A}}{8}$ atoms.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
The Bohr radius of a hydrogen like species is 70.53 pm . The species and the stationary state (n) are respectively

(Given : Hydrogen atom Bohr radius is 52.9 pm )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that the radius of any hydrogen-like species is given by the formula:

$r_{\text{species}}=a_{0}\frac{n^{2}}{Z}$

Here, $a_{0}$ is the Bohr radius of hydrogen (given as 52.9 pm), $n$ is the principal quantum number, and $Z$ is the atomic number of the nucleus.

Substituting the given values:

$70.53=52.9\left (\frac{n^{2}}{Z}\right )$

Now, divide both sides by 52.9:

$\frac{n^{2}}{Z}=\frac{70.53}{52.9}=1.33\approx \frac{4}{3}$

To make the fraction $\frac{n^{2}}{Z}=\frac{4}{3}$, we can take $n=2$ (so $n^{2}=4$) and $Z=3$.

Thus, the species is $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ and the electron is in the $n=2$ energy level.

$\mathrm{Li}^{2+},n=2\Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}=1.33$

text:
Match List - I with List - II.

Given $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ are initial and final volumes respectively.

  

    List - I
(Isothermal process)

    List - II
(Expression)

  

  

    A.

    Reversible
expansion

    I.

    $\mathrm{q}=0$

  

  

    B.

    Free expansion

    II.

    $\mathrm{q}=\mathrm{nRT}\ln \frac{\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{V}_{1}}$

  

  

    C.

    Irreversible
Compression

    III.

    $\mathrm{w}=-\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathrm{V}_{1}-\mathrm{V}_{2})$

  

  

    D.

    Cyclic reversible

    IV.

    $\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{rev}}}{\mathrm{T}}=0$

  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Reversible isothermal expansion

For an ideal gas in a reversible and isothermal expansion:

$w=-nRT\ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}$

Since the process is isothermal,  

$\Delta U=0⟹q=-w$

Hence,

$q=nRT\ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}$

Therefore, A corresponds to II.

(B) Free expansion

In free expansion, gas expands against zero external pressure:

$p_{\text{ext}}=0$

Thus,

$w=0\text{and}q=0$

(Also, for an ideal gas, ΔU = 0.)

Therefore, B corresponds to I.

(C) Irreversible isothermal compression

For irreversible compression (against constant external pressure):

$w=-p_{\text{ext}}(V_{1}-V_{2})$

Therefore, C corresponds to III.

(D) Cyclic reversible process

For a cyclic reversible process:

$\int \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}=0$

Therefore, D corresponds to IV.

Correct Option: (C)  

$A-II,B-I,C-III,D-IV$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :


[IMG]

Statement I : $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ molecules move from the chamber 1 to chamber 2 .

Statement II : The osmotic pressure of a solution prepared by dissolving 50 mg of potassium sulphate (molar mass $=174\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$ ) in 2 L of water (at $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ ) is 0.0107 bar. (Given: $\mathrm{R}=0.083\mathrm{dm}^{3}$ bar $\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and assume complete dissociation of electrolyte)

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In chamber (I), the concentration of solute is calculated as:

$C_{1}=\frac{18/180}{0.1}=1\text{M}$

In chamber (II), the concentration is given by:

$C_{2}=\frac{30/180}{250/1000}=\frac{2}{3}\text{M}$

Since osmotic pressure depends on concentration and $π_{1}>π_{2}$, water will move from the side having lower osmotic pressure (chamber II) to the side having higher osmotic pressure (chamber I).

Osmotic pressure is calculated using the formula:

$π=iCRT$

For potassium sulfate $(\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4})$, the van’t Hoff factor is $i=3$.

So,

$π=3\times \left (\frac{50\times 10^{-3}/174}{2}\right )\times 0.083\times 300$

On solving,

$π=0.0107\text{bar}$

text: Given is a concentrated solution of a weak electrolyte $A_{x}B_{y}$ of concentration ' $c$ ' and dissociation constant ' K '. The degree of dissociation is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the weak electrolyte $A_{x}B_{y}$ dissociate in water as follows:

$A_{x}B_{y}⇌xA^{y+}+yB^{x-}$

Let the initial concentration of $A_{x}B_{y}$ be $c$, and let the degree of dissociation be $α$.

At equilibrium,

Concentration of undissociated $A_{x}B_{y}=c(1-α)$

Concentration of $A^{y+}=cxα$

Concentration of $B^{x-}=cyα$

$K=\frac{[A^{y+}]^{x}[B^{x-}]^{y}}{[A_{x}B_{y}]}$

Substituting equilibrium concentrations:

$K=\frac{(cxα)^{x}(cyα)^{y}}{c(1-α)}$

Simplify:

$K=c^{x+y-1}x^{x}y^{y}\frac{α^{x+y}}{1-α}$

Since the solution is concentrated, $α$ is small, but generally in such problems the expression is kept exact. However, for simplification, at high concentration the term $(1-α)\approx 1$ is often used if it is a weak electrolyte.

So approximately:

$K\approx c^{x+y-1}x^{x}y^{y}α^{x+y}$

$α^{x+y}=\frac{K}{c^{x+y-1}x^{x}y^{y}}$

$α=\left (\frac{K}{c^{x+y-1}x^{x}y^{y}}\right )^{\frac{1}{x+y}}$

This matches Option B:

$α=\left (\dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1}x^{x}y^{y}}\right )^{\frac{1}{x+y}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
For a general redox reaction

Anode $\mathrm{Red}_{1}\to \mathrm{Ox}_{1}^{\mathrm{n}_{1}^{+}}+\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{e}^{-}$

Cathode $\mathrm{O}x_{2}+\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Red}_{2}^{\mathrm{n}_{2}-}$

Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: The overall reaction can be written as $\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{Red}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{O}x_{2}⇌\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{O}x_{1}^{\mathrm{n}_{1}^{+}}+\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{Red}_{2}^{\mathrm{n}_{2}^{-}}$

The electrons do not appear in the overall reaction because electrons produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode.


[IMG]
Here $n$ is the number of electrons transferred in redox reaction.
If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll}  \\ \begin{array}{ll} (a)Anode: & \left (Red1⟶O_{x_{1}}^{n^{+}}+n_{1}e^{-}\right )\cdot n_{2} \\ \left (Ox_{2}+n_{2}e^{-}⟶\mathrm{Red}_{2}^{n_{2}^{-}}\right )\cdot n_{1} \end{array} \end{array}$

To add the anode and cathode half-reactions, the number of electrons must be the same on both sides.

So, we multiply the anode reaction by $n_{2}$ and the cathode reaction by $n_{1}$, so that both have $n_{1}n_{2}$ electrons.

$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} n_{2}\mathrm{Red}_{1}⟶n_{2}\mathrm{Ox}_{1}^{n+}+n_{2}n_{1}e^{-} \\ n_{1}\mathrm{Ox}_{2}+n_{1}n_{2}e^{-}⟶n_{1}\mathrm{Red}_{2}^{n_{2}-} \end{array} \\ \text{Overall reaction:}n_{2}Red+n_{1}Ox_{2}⟶n_{2}Ox^{n+}+n_{1}Red_{2}^{n_{2}-} \end{array}$

Now, when we add these two equations, the $n_{1}n_{2}e^{-}$ on the product side of the anode reaction cancels with the $n_{1}n_{2}e^{-}$ on the reactant side of the cathode reaction.

(b) The $e^{-}$produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode, that's why $e^{-}$do not appear in the overall reaction.

This statement is correct because electrons cancel during addition of the two half-reactions.

(c) We know,

$\begin{array}{l} E=E^{o}-\dfrac{RT}{nF}\log Q \\ E-E^{\circ }=\dfrac{-RT}{nF}\log Q \\ \dfrac{E-E^{\circ }}{RT/F}=-\dfrac{1}{n}\log Q \end{array}$

Here, $E$ changes with $\log Q$ according to the Nernst equation, and $n$ is the number of electrons transferred in the balanced redox reaction.

plotting a $y=mx+c$ graph,

$\begin{array}{l} y=\dfrac{E-E^{0}}{RT/F} \\ x=\log Q \\ \text{slope}(m)=-\dfrac{1}{n} \\ \text{slope}\propto \dfrac{1}{n} \end{array}$

So, the slope is $-\frac{1}{n}$. This statement is also correct.

$\text{Where,}n=\text{no. of}e^{-}\text{transferred in redox reaction.}$

(D) The electrical work done by a galvanic cell is given by the product of the total charge transferred and the potential difference, not their ratio.

This statement is correct because electrical work is given by $W=qV$ (charge multiplied by potential difference).

$\begin{array}{ll} W_{electrical} & =\text{charge × Potential difference.} \\ =Q\times V \end{array}$

                $W_{e}=It\times V$

text: In a period, the first ionisation enthalpy of the element at extreme left and the negative electron gain enthalpy of the extreme right element, except noble gases, are respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The element on the far left of a period belongs to Group 1. These elements have only one electron in their outermost shell, so they lose this electron easily. Therefore, they have the lowest first ionisation enthalpy (IE).

The element on the far right of a period, except noble gases, belongs to Group 17 (halogens). These atoms need just one electron to complete their outermost shell, so they strongly attract an extra electron. Hence, they have the most negative value of electron gain enthalpy ($\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{eg}}$).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $\mathrm{F}_{2}\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is the correct trend in terms of bond angle.

Statement II : $\mathrm{SiF}_{4},\mathrm{SnF}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{PbF}_{4}$ are ionic in nature.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ the oxygen atom is $sp^{3}$ hybridised with 2 bp + 2 lp, so the bond angle depends on the bonded atoms.

In $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ the highly electronegative F atoms draw the bonding pairs away from O, bond pair–bond pair repulsion is small and the angle is about $103^{\circ }$.

In $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ the bonding pairs lie closer to O, so the angle is larger, $104.5^{\circ }$.

In $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ the large Cl atoms repel each other and the bonding pairs lie closer to the more electronegative O, so the angle opens to about $111^{\circ }$.

The order $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is correct, so Statement I is true.

Among the group 14 tetrafluorides, $\mathrm{SnF}{}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{PbF}{}_{4}$ are ionic, but $\mathrm{SiF}{}_{4}$ is a covalent molecular gas, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
The correct order of first $(\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{1})$ and second $(\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{2})$ ionisation enthalpy values of Cr and Mn are :

A. $\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{1}:\mathrm{Cr}>\mathrm{Mn}$

B. $\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{2}:\mathrm{Cr}>\mathrm{Mn}$

C. $\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{1}:\mathrm{Mn}>\mathrm{Cr}$

D. $\Delta _{i}\mathrm{H}_{2}:\mathrm{Mn}>\mathrm{Cr}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cr (Z = 24):  

Ground state configuration:  

$\mathrm{Cr}:[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$  

(due to extra stability of half-filled $3d^{5}$ and $4s^{1}$ configuration)

Mn (Z = 25):  

Ground state configuration:  

$\mathrm{Mn}:[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{2}$  

First ionisation enthalpy, $\Delta _{i}H_{1}$
In the first ionisation process:

Cr:  

$\mathrm{Cr}\to \mathrm{Cr}^{+}+e^{-}$  

After removal of one 4s electron:  

$\mathrm{Cr}^{+}:[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}$ (a very stable half-filled configuration)

Mn:  

$\mathrm{Mn}\to \mathrm{Mn}^{+}+e^{-}$  

After removal of one 4s electron:  

$\mathrm{Mn}^{+}:[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$ (not as stable as half-filled 3d⁵ only)

Because the resulting $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$ ion is particularly stable, less energy is required to form $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$, i.e.

$\Delta _{i}H_{1}(\mathrm{Cr})<\Delta _{i}H_{1}(\mathrm{Mn})$

Thus,

Correct order for first ionisation enthalpy:  

$\Delta _{i}H_{1}:\mathrm{Mn}>\mathrm{Cr}$

(Corresponds to option C.)

Second ionisation enthalpy, $\Delta _{i}H_{2}$
Now, let us remove the second electron.

Cr:  

From the already stable $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$ ($[Ar]3d^{5}$):  

$\mathrm{Cr}^{+}\to \mathrm{Cr}^{2+}+e^{-}$  

After this, $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ becomes:  

$[Ar]3d^{4}$ — less stable.  

Therefore, it requires a large amount of energy to remove this second electron.

Mn:  

From $\mathrm{Mn}^{+}$ ($[Ar]3d^{5}4s^{1}$):  

$\mathrm{Mn}^{+}\to \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+e^{-}$  

After this, $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ becomes:  

$[Ar]3d^{5}$ — a stable half-filled configuration.  

Thus, less energy is needed for the second ionisation.

Hence,

$\Delta _{i}H_{2}(\mathrm{Cr})>\Delta _{i}H_{2}(\mathrm{Mn})$

which corresponds to option B.

Combine results

$\Delta _{i}H_{1}$: Mn > Cr  → option C  

$\Delta _{i}H_{2}$: Cr > Mn  → option B

Therefore, the correct combination is:

$\text{B and C only}$

Final Answer: Option B
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Which of the following sequences of hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature are correct for the given coordination compounds?

A. $[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-}-\mathrm{sp}^{3}$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic

B. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}-\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$, octahedral, paramagnetic

C. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}]-\mathrm{sp}^{3}$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic

D. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}-\mathrm{dsp}^{2}$, square planar, diamagnetic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ni ($Z=28$) is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{8}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$.

A. $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so $3d^{8}$ keeps 2 unpaired electrons and the $4s$ and $4p$ orbitals give $sp^{3}$: tetrahedral and paramagnetic. Statement A is correct.


[IMG]

B. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: even after pairing, a $3d^{8}$ ion can vacate only one $3d$ orbital, so six ligand pairs must use $4s$, $4p$ and two $4d$ orbitals: $sp^{3}d^{2}$, octahedral, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$ with 2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic. Statement B is correct.

C. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: the strong field ligand CO makes $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{0}$ $3d^{10}4s^{0}$, and the $4s$ and $4p$ orbitals give $sp^{3}$, tetrahedral, with no unpaired electron, so the complex is diamagnetic. Statement C is incorrect.


[IMG]

D. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: the strong field ligand $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the eight $3d$ electrons into four orbitals, leaving one $3d$ orbital for $dsp^{2}$ hybridisation: square planar and diamagnetic. Statement D is correct.


[IMG]

Statements A, B and D are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : A mixture of $\mathrm{C}_{12}\mathrm{H}_{22}\mathrm{O}_{11}$ (sugar) and NaCl can be separated by dissolving sugar in alcohol, due to differential solubility.

Statement II : Rose essence from rose petals is seperated by steam distillation due to its high volatility and insolubility in $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sugar dissolves in alcohol, but NaCl (common salt) does not dissolve in alcohol.

Therefore, the mixture of sugar and salt can be separated using a process called solvent extraction or differential extraction, based on their different solubilities in alcohol.

Rose essence (essential oil) is volatile with steam, meaning it can evaporate with steam. Hence, it is separated from rose petals by the method of steam distillation.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Shown below is the structure of methyl acetate with three different $α,β$ and $γ$ carbon - oxygen bonds.


[IMG]


The correct order of bond lengths of these bonds is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In methyl acetate, $α$ is the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ bond, $β$ is the bond between the carbonyl carbon and the ester oxygen, and $γ$ is the bond between that oxygen and the methyl carbon.

A lone pair of the ester oxygen is delocalised into the carbonyl group:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(-\mathrm{O}{}^{-})=\mathrm{O}{}^{+}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$

The neutral first structure contributes more, so $α$ keeps most of its double-bond character and is the shortest.

$β$ gains partial double-bond character, so it is shorter than an ordinary $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond.

$γ$ takes no part in the resonance and remains a pure $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond, so it is the longest.

Bond length order: $α<β<γ$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: ' $x$ ' is the product which is obtained by the hydrolysis of prop-1-yne in the presence of mercuric sulphate under dilute acidic medium at 333 K . ' $y$ ' is the product which is obtained by the reaction of ethane nitrile with methyl magnesium bromide in dry ether followed by hydrolysis. IUPAC name of product obtained from ' $x$ ' and ' $y$ ' in the presence of barium hydroxide followed by heating is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydration of propyne with $\mathrm{HgSO}{}_{4}$ in dilute $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ follows Markovnikov's rule; the enol $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ tautomerises to propanone, so $x$ is $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ adds to the $\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ of ethanenitrile to give $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{NMgBr}$, which hydrolyses to propanone, so $y$ is also $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$.

With $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}$ two molecules of propanone undergo aldol addition to give 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one, which loses water on heating:

$2~\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}{}^{\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}{}^{\Delta }(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CHCOCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Numbering from the end nearer the carbonyl puts $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ at C2, $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ at C3 and the methyl group at C4, so the product is 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (mesityl oxide).

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Consider the following organic reaction sequence. Choose the final product $(X)$ from the following (consider the major product in all intermediate reactions)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Propanoic acid with $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ forms ammonium propanoate, which loses water on heating to give propanamide:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}{}^{\Delta }\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

NaOH/$\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ (Hofmann bromamide degradation) removes the carbonyl carbon and gives ethylamine:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}+4\mathrm{NaOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaBr}+\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ in water at $0{}^{\circ }\text{C}$ converts the primary aliphatic amine, through its unstable diazonium ion, into ethanol:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{N}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Ethanol reduces benzenediazonium chloride, replacing $-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ by H, and is itself oxidised to ethanal:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}+\mathrm{N}{}_{2}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{HCl}$

So X is benzene; phenol would need the diazonium salt to be warmed with water.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with $\mathrm{Br}_{2}/\mathrm{KOH}$ (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}/\mathrm{KOH}$ (Hofmann bromamide degradation) converts only primary amides $\mathrm{RCONH}{}_{2}$ into primary amines $\mathrm{RNH}{}_{2}$ with one carbon atom less. The N-substituted amides $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{CONHCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{CCONHCH}{}_{3}$ do not give this reaction.

The four primary amides give: $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ to aniline $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ to benzylamine $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ to methylamine $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, and $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ to cyclohexylamine $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$.

Gabriel phthalimide synthesis gives primary aliphatic amines by nucleophilic substitution of an alkyl halide by the phthalimide anion followed by hydrolysis: benzyl chloride, methyl iodide and cyclohexyl bromide give benzylamine, methylamine and cyclohexylamine respectively.

Aniline cannot be obtained by Gabriel synthesis, because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

So 3 compounds satisfy both conditions.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Treatment of a gas ' $X$ ' with a freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution gives a compound ' $Y$ ' as a brown ring. The compounds X and Y are:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The reaction described is the well-known brown ring test, which is a confirmatory test for nitrate ions ($NO_{3}^{-}$). Let's understand the chemistry behind it.

Understanding the Reactants:

The test uses a freshly prepared solution of ferrous sulphate ($FeSO_{4}$). It needs to be fresh because the ferrous ion ($Fe^{2+}$) can be easily oxidized to ferric ion ($Fe^{3+}$) by the oxygen in the air.

The question mentions a gas 'X' is treated with this solution. In a standard brown ring test, this gas is produced in situ (within the reaction mixture). Let's see how.

Formation of Gas 'X':

The test is for nitrate ions ($NO_{3}^{-}$). In an acidic medium (usually provided by adding concentrated $H_{2}SO_{4}$), the nitrate ion oxidizes the ferrous ion ($Fe^{2+}$) to ferric ion ($Fe^{3+}$), and in the process, the nitrate ion itself gets reduced to nitric oxide ($NO$).

The balanced ionic equation is:

$NO_{3}^{-}+3Fe^{2+}+4H^{+}⟶NO+3Fe^{3+}+2H_{2}O$

So, the gas 'X' that is formed is nitric oxide, $NO$.

Formation of the Brown Ring (Compound 'Y'):

The nitric oxide ($NO$) gas produced then reacts with the excess ferrous ions ($Fe^{2+}$) present in the solution to form a coordination complex. This complex has a characteristic brown colour.

The reaction is:

$[Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}+NO⟶[Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}+H_{2}O$

This brown-coloured complex is pentaaquanitrosyliron(II) ion. The complete compound 'Y' is pentaaquanitrosyliron(II) sulphate, with the formula $[Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]SO_{4}$.

For simplicity in the options, the water ligands are often omitted, and the compound is written as $[Fe(NO)]SO_{4}$.

Conclusion:

The gas 'X' is nitric oxide, $NO$.

The brown compound 'Y' is the complex $[Fe(NO)]SO_{4}$.

Looking at the options, we can see that Option A matches our findings.

Therefore, the correct option is A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
An excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ is added to 100 mL of a 0.05 M solution of tetraaquadichloridochromium (III) chloride. The number of moles of AgCl precipitated will be $____$ $\times 10^{-3}$.

(Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given complex is $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}$.

When an excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ is added, the $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ion outside the coordination sphere reacts with $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ to form a white precipitate of silver chloride ($\mathrm{AgCl}$).

The reaction is:

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\to [\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]\mathrm{NO}_{3}+\mathrm{AgCl}↓$

From the reaction, 1 mole of the complex gives 1 mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$.

Now, the number of moles of the given complex is calculated as:

$\text{Moles of complex}=M\times V=0.05\times 100\times 10^{-3}=5\times 10^{-3}\text{moles}$

Hence, moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ formed $=5\times 10^{-3}$ moles.

Therefore, the required value of $x=5$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: An alkane $(Y)$ requires 8 moles of oxygen for complete combustion and on chlorination with $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}/\mathrm{h}ν,(\mathrm{Y})$ gives only one monochlorinated product $(\mathrm{Z})$. The total number of primary carbon atoms in $(Y)$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Complete combustion of an alkane $\mathrm{C}_{n}\mathrm{H}_{2n+2}$:

$\mathrm{C}_{n}\mathrm{H}_{2n+2}+\dfrac{3n+1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}\to n\mathrm{CO}_{2}+(n+1)\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\dfrac{3n+1}{2}=8\Rightarrow 3n+1=16\Rightarrow n=5$, so (Y) is $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}$. A cycloalkane $\mathrm{C}_{n}\mathrm{H}_{2n}$ would need $\dfrac{3n}{2}=8$, which gives no whole number of carbon atoms.

Of the three isomers of $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}$, n-pentane gives 3 and isopentane gives 4 monochloro products; only neopentane, $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{4}$, has all 12 H atoms equivalent and gives the single product $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$ with $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}/hν$.

In neopentane, each of the four $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carbons is bonded to only one carbon (primary), and the central carbon is quaternary.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: 500 mL of $0.2\mathrm{M}\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ solution in basic medium when mixed with 500 mL of 1.5 M KI solution, oxidises iodide ions to liberate molecular iodine. This liberated iodine is then titrated with a standard $x\mathrm{M}$ thiosulphate solution in presence of starch till the end point. If 300 mL of thiosulphate was consumed, then the value of $x$ is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In basic medium iodide reduces permanganate to $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ (Mn: $+7\to +4$), so the n-factor of $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$ is 3; iodide ($-1\to 0$) has n-factor 1.

$\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+3\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+4\mathrm{OH}{}^{-},2~\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{I}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$

Equivalents of $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}=0.2\times 0.5\times 3=0.3$; equivalents of $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}=1.5\times 0.5\times 1=0.75$.

$\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$ is the limiting reagent, so the iodine liberated is 0.3 equivalent ($0.15\text{mol}\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$).

In the titration $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}+\qquad 2\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{I}{}^{-}+\mathrm{S}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}{}^{2-}$ each thiosulphate ion gives one electron (n-factor 1). By the law of equivalence, equivalents of $\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ = equivalents of $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ = equivalents of $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$:

$x\times \dfrac{300}{1000}\times 1=0.3\Rightarrow x=1$

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Decomposition of a hydrocarbon follows the equation $\mathrm{k}=\left (5.5\times 10^{11}\mathrm{s}^{-1}\right )\mathrm{e}^{\frac{-28000\mathrm{K}}{\mathrm{T}}}$. The activation energy of reaction is $____$ $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)

Given : $\mathrm{R}=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given the Arrhenius equation in the exponential form:

$k=Ae^{-\frac{Ea}{RT}}$

Comparing this with the given equation:

$k=(5.5\times 10^{11}\text{s}^{-1})e^{-\frac{28000}{T}}$

we can see that:

$\frac{E_{a}}{R}=28000$

Now, substituting the given value of the gas constant $R=8.3\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$:

$E_{a}=28000\times 8.3\text{J mol}^{-1}$

$E_{a}=232400\text{J mol}^{-1}$

Converting joules to kilojoules:

$E_{a}=\frac{232400}{1000}=232.4\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to the nearest integer:

$E_{a}=232\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
